slides.subtitle:
Six samples can tell different stories.
Invented synthetic river signals; no field observations.
slides.notes: There is no named river, geographical coordinate, measured environmental event, pollutant concentration or regulatory criterion. All time values are dimensionless toy time units and all responses are arbitrary units.

slides.interpretation: An uneventful sampled line is compatible with an unsampled peak.
slides.notes: This one-figure ledger allows a large evidence region rather than a dense thumbnail inventory. The visible native caption is an interpretation ledger, not an external citation. Sample markers encode schedules as well as color.

slides.title: A phase shift changes retained peak height
slides.subtitle: Synthetic mean retained peak fraction; 24 paired realizations per schedule
slides.caption: SYN-R. Fraction = sampled peak above baseline / dense-grid peak above baseline. Zero-based bar axis.
slides.notes: Compute a ratio per realization before averaging. The paired schedules have identical six-value budgets. Each realization perturbs pulse centers by seeded Gaussian jitter with SD 1.5 toy time units. This statistic is peak retention, not event detection sensitivity, exposure, pollutant load or confidence in absence. B is aligned to the generator by design.

slides.title: Averages do not erase the alignment advantage
slides.subtitle: All 24 paired synthetic ratios, not just the two means

slides.summary_callout: Invented signals illustrate a sampling blind spot. No field finding has been established.
slides.notes: No actual river, instrument, station, date, water-quality measurement or field asset was used. The proposed random-timing experiment is not included in the current generator. Reproducibility of the toy result is not general validation of phase B.
